title: SQL injection
flaw: The isolated demonstration concatenates SQL; the normal route uses bound parameters.
scenario: If search concatenates input, a crafted query can bypass record filtering and disclose nonpublic research metadata. Successful SQL injection depends on the actual query and database grants.
control: Parameterized search and publication filtering; synthetic exploit comparison and regression tests pass.
status: Demonstrated in isolated vulnerable example; mitigated in normal application

title: Object authorization bypass
flaw: Omitting per-record authorization would expose another user record; current predicates reject that access.
scenario: A user changes a record ID and reads another research team’s nonpublic record or service request. Client-hidden links do not enforce authorization.
control: Owner-or-staff predicates on records; default denial; cross-user tests pass. Collaborator grants are not implemented.

title: Backup confidentiality exposure
flaw: Temporary pg_dump copies are not encrypted by the application; a local user able to read them can recover records.
scenario: An operator mishandles a local recovery copy or exposes it through filesystem permissions; no cloud bucket or public export endpoint is assumed.
control: Temporary-directory cleanup and controlled operator access; application backup encryption and custody evidence remain proposed.
status: Current residual risk; no application-level dump encryption

title: Committed credentials
stride: Spoofing; Information disclosure; Elevation of privilege
flaw: Accidental committed credentials can be copied from Git history; hooks can be bypassed, so CI is independently required.
scenario: A repository reader obtains a secret and impersonates a service if network access and credential permissions permit. Removing the file alone does not revoke a leaked secret.
control: Pre-commit rejection, Gitleaks CI and protected branches; rotate any real leaked credential. Native private-repo push protection unavailable.
status: Mitigated scenario; fake-secret rejection and CI verified

title: Missing database isolation
agent: Authenticated peer exploiting another query flaw
flaw: Runtime role can select multiple users rows; application predicates are the isolation boundary and a future missed query could bypass it.
scenario: A missed application permission check exposes rows across research groups. Missing RLS is a defense gap, not by itself proof that a user can query the database.
control: Non-owner runtime and tested application predicates; RLS not implemented.
status: Current residual risk; runtime role is not row-isolated

title: Session interception
flaw: Local HTTP carries bearer credentials without TLS; deployment on an untrusted network would expose them.
scenario: A victim uses an insecure session path and an observer obtains a usable session. Ordinary Wi-Fi visibility does not decrypt correctly validated HTTPS.
control: Hashed expiring bearer sessions and revocation; local HTTP only. Production HTTPS remains required. No cookie authentication.
status: Current transport limitation; local HTTP only

title: Loss of recovery copies under extortion
flaw: Backup exercise has no independent immutable recovery generation; compromise of the same operator host may destroy both data and reachable copies.
scenario: An extortionist who already controls the operator host removes or encrypts reachable recovery copies; no upload or parser feature is assumed.
control: Verified local restore is a prerequisite, not offsite resilience. Proposed immutable independent recovery, segregated credentials and rehearsed incident recovery.
status: Current recovery design gap; extortion is a hypothetical scenario

title: Database extortion
agent: Ransomware operator with credentials or DB exploit
stride: Denial of service; Tampering; Information disclosure
flaw: A stolen administrator credential can alter research data; runtime restriction does not constrain the separately privileged setup identity.
scenario: After developer-host compromise, an attacker reuses available administrator credentials against the local database and encrypts or destroys A-02.
control: Separate non-owner runtime, loopback DB and tested restore; protect setup credentials and add independent immutable backups before production.
status: Current privileged-account threat scenario; compromise not demonstrated

title: Resource exhaustion
flaw: Without bounds, search and graph processing can exhaust resources; current route caps and worker lifecycle limits mitigate that case.
scenario: Authenticated staff floods costly graph-solving scenarios or clients flood search. Unbounded child processes would exhaust host resources.
control: Rate/body limits; staff-only solver; 5000 steps, 25000 edges, 50000 memberships, 2 MiB body; two Python workers, five-second timeout, 8 MiB output ceiling. No OS memory sandbox.
status: Mitigated resource scenario; OS/distributed limits remain

title: Malformed worker certificate
flaw: Status-only worker validation accepted incomplete SUCCESS objects before correction.
scenario: A faulty or compromised Python worker sends a superficially successful but malformed certificate. Express must reject it before presenting a result.
control: Full structural/type/membership validation; malformed object yields WORKER_PROTOCOL/502; worker process is bounded.
status: Demonstrated boundary defect; corrected and regression tested

title: Unattributable record changes
flaw: Runtime audit grants prevent modification, but the database owner can still alter or delete audit events.
scenario: A privileged administrator changes database state and erases local audit traces. No nonexistent research-update API is assumed.
control: Runtime INSERT/SELECT-only audit grants tested; external tamper-resistant audit storage and administrator oversight remain proposed.
status: Current residual risk; administrator can alter audit history
